source_observations.observation: Upa is coupled to proximity and adhi to elevation in a mountain name. Kāśikā attributes retention of a to the name restriction. Tattva cites the specific exclusion for tyakan.

source_observations.locator: Amarakośa, Śailavarga with Dakṣiṇātya commentary, printed p. 214
source_observations.observation: The glosses distinguish land close to a mountain and land on it above.
Hermitages are visible in the lower mountain sites. Upatyakā has the plural locative ending.
The upper site is locative singular within a simile. The commentator explicitly cites 5.2.34. He distinguishes readings with double l and with lt on the flowering lodhra tree.
The noun karman is locative. Ghaṭ refers to making effort. Bālā invokes loss of the final ṭi and accounts for the preserved ṭh.
Taddhita supplies the conditioning environment for the loss on n-final karman.
The thing arisen supplies the nominative input. The bearer supplies the genitive relation. The commentary distinguishes hunger or thirst now from a past desiderative analysis, and rice from the cow.
The compound with flowering trees is masculine singular and describes the mountain Ṛṣyamūka in relation to Pampā.
Feminine accusative puṣpitām agrees with speech. The verb with pra has a third plural active ending.
Quotes the opening words of 5.2.36, names tārakādi and itac and explains the transfer from visible flowers to attractive speech.
Aja, waiting near the city, is the accusative participant. The king of Vidarbha goes out to meet him. The same strong participle in 2.29 describes the lion.
The addressee has attained all good things. Adhijagmuṣaḥ agrees with the possessive te, glossed tava.

source_observations.locator: Prauḍhamanoramā on the Kaumudī entry under 6.4.131
source_observations.observation: Quotes both fifth-canto passages, distinguishes poets’ usage and proposes a limited explanation through occasional chandas forms in bhāṣā.
The named ordinary speech provision gives sad, vas and śru. The registry has kvasuś ca at 3.2.107, although the displayed commentary at Raghuvaṃśa 2.29 attaches the number 3.2.102.
Records iṭ with the relevant ā-final base in front of vas. Compare the weak uṣ of the distinct gam genitive under 6.4.131.
The periphrastic desiderative is a distinct previously owned request. The simple active perfect provides jagāma here.
Distinguished in the lexical source from curādi 10.0379 vad in communicating a message.
